- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model often underestimates; adjust upward slightly to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings — if sentiment shifts sharply, delay forecast adjustment until 2–3 days later to avoid overshoot.
- In low-volatility periods, model tends to underestimate mean reversion; add a small upward bias to forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion after a spike, model often fails to correct — apply a “lag correction” by smoothing out the forecast’s immediate drop after a peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates the “tail” of the price path — especially when sentiment is mixed — add a small upward bias toward end of forecast window.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction — align forecast slope with sentiment trend, not just magnitude.
